about.title: Beyond the
paragraphs: I'm a data scientist with a background in statistics. What I enjoy most about my work is finding ways to use data and apply statistical methods to turn it into information that helps people make decisions.

I also enjoy working with people who know the business and are willing to share that context. Understanding how they work, what they need and what they expect from the results helps me choose better methods, identify which information matters and build solutions that truly answer their needs.

I like exploring different methods and learning from the variety of problems that can be tackled with data. In the end, something I value about this profession is that data science can be applied in many sectors, as long as there is a real need and a willingness to work together.

items.text: Lead prioritization with a classifier above 70 % precision and churn prediction with survival analysis, in production with Python, dbt, Snowflake and AWS.
Customer profiles and market baskets; a recommendation system with PySpark to personalize the product portfolio. Presented results to management.
Customer segmentation applied to 80 % of the client base, KPI dashboards in Power BI and automation of 50 % of the models.

items.role: Analytics analyst, junior and then semi-senior
items.text: Purchase prediction models and recommendation systems for consumer goods clients. The prediction model was adopted by more than 30 % of the clients.

projects.title: What I build to keep
projects.lead: Exercises and technical challenges with public or test data, which I use to practice and stay up to date.
projects.leadMuted: All the code is open on GitHub; the metrics are those of the exercise.

items.title: AWS pipeline and delivery-delay model
items.tag: AWS · PySpark · SageMaker · Olist public dataset
items.text: I integrated 99,441 orders from seven sources into an analytics layer (S3, Glue, Athena), trained an XGBoost model in SageMaker to estimate which orders will arrive late, and orchestrated the flow with Step Functions.
items.imageAlt: Step Functions state machine of the pipeline

items.title: Classic ML versus an LLM on price anomalies
items.text: I compared Isolation Forest with an LLM on price series per product and measured the difference with an A/B test. In the same challenge, PageRank on a graph of pages and a RAG with a critic agent.

items.title: Customer churn from purchase history
items.text: Recency, amount, frequency and periodicity features for 80,294 customers; class balanced with SMOTE and six models compared with cross-validation. XGBoost won by a clear margin.
items.imageAlt: Comparison of six models by metric

items.title: Cost forecasting for construction equipment
items.text: From raw-material prices I projected equipment costs with OLS and ARIMA, added intervals with Monte Carlo simulation, and left a conversational agent to ask about the forecast.
items.imageAlt: Forecast steps: raw materials, feature selection, OLS and ARIMA, Monte Carlo, agent

tools.title: What I work
tools.lead: Python and R to model, SQL for the data, Snowflake, dbt and PySpark to move it, AWS to put it in production, and Power BI or QuickSight to tell the story.
